expectations.evidence: Lines 16-43 detail all current capabilities: L7 content switching, SSL offloading, GSLB with MEP, WAF/AppFW, health monitoring, CPX K8s ingress, NITRO API automation, ACI Service Graph integration, and infrastructure scale (30 vservers, 4 HA pairs, 2 DCs).

Lines 72-91 provide detailed capability mapping table: iRules/LTM Policies vs Responder/Rewrite, ASM/AWAF vs AppFW (lines 125-132 expand WAF comparison), BIG-IP DNS vs GSLB (lines 113-121), plus iQuery vs MEP, AS3 vs NITRO.

Lines 196-213 map every NetScaler feature to HAProxy equivalents, explicitly marking GSLB and WAF as 'NOT BUILT-IN' with High migration complexity. Three-way feature comparison table at lines 383-395 reinforces what HAProxy can and cannot replace.

Lines 229-254 present four GSLB options: PowerDNS with custom health glue, Consul, external DNS (Cloudflare/Route53), or keep NetScaler for GSLB only. BIG-IP DNS covered at lines 113-121. Recommendation provided for each migration path.

Lines 256-281 cover ModSecurity SPOE, Coraza, open-appsec, and dedicated WAF layer options for HAProxy. F5 ASM/AWAF comparison at lines 125-132. Staying on AppFW addressed in Option 3. Performance overhead (10-30%) noted for ModSecurity.

F5 CIS detailed at lines 136-141 (noting external proxy model vs in-cluster CPX, latency concerns, SPK mention). HAProxy Ingress Controller at lines 286-291 with Envoy/Contour/Traefik alternatives. CPX modernization in Option 3 at line 351.

Lines 95-109 detail F5 ACI device package migration: installing device package on APIC, registering devices, creating new Service Graph templates, migrating function profiles, updating Contracts, testing PBR. HAProxy explicitly noted as having no Service Graph support (line 226).

Lines 438-513 define a 5-phase, 24-week migration plan: Phase 0 assessment/lab (weeks 1-4), Phase 1 infrastructure (weeks 5-8), Phase 2 four migration waves by risk (weeks 9-20), Phase 3 K8s ingress (weeks 16-22), Phase 4 decommission (weeks 21-24). Explicitly not big-bang.

Lines 215-227 cover Octavia deployment: amphora vs OVN provider drivers, ACI interaction (amphorae as OpFlex endpoints), lb-mgmt-net, no ACI Service Graph support, VIP placement on provider networks. Recommendation to use amphora driver for L7.

Three separate cost tables (F5 lines 153-164, HAProxy lines 301-316, NetScaler lines 365-375) with line items for licensing, hardware/compute, migration effort, training, support, and ongoing ops. 5-year TCO projection at lines 412-419 comparing all three options.

F5 automation at lines 145-151 (AS3, DO, TS, Ansible f5_modules, Terraform). HAProxy automation at lines 294-299 (Octavia API, Ansible openstack.cloud, Terraform openstack provider). NITRO modernization in Option 3 lines 347-348. Code examples in Appendix B for all three platforms.

Lines 519-555: Primary recommendation is Stay on NetScaler with 5 stated rationales (lowest risk, ACI Service Graph, GSLB gap, competitive TCO, modernization value). Secondary recommendation F5 if vendor change mandated. HAProxy conditions clearly stated. Weighted decision matrix at lines 421-433.
